page: Microsoft Azure D64d_v4 is a general-purpose server instance belonging to the DDv4 family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features 64 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 32 physical cores of an Intel Xeon 8272CL processor operating at 2.6 GHz. The x86_64 architecture includes 32 KB L1d cache, 1.0 MB L2 cache, and 35 MB L3 cache. Memory capacity is 256.0 GB, yielding a balanced 4.0 GB of RAM per core. The instance is equipped with 2458 GB of bundled local SSD storage, while containing zero GPUs and zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark results show strong performance in memory operations and database tasks. The instance achieves top 25% results in large-block read-only memory bandwidth (208.41 GB/sec) and large-block write memory bandwidth (93.84 GB/sec), alongside a strong PassMark memory score of 2769.97. PassMark database operations also rank in the top 25% at 22475.92. Standard CPU benchmarks, such as stress-ng single-core (1485.29) and multi-core (59579.33), fall within the average range.

While the server demonstrates strong memory bandwidth and database processing capabilities, it exhibits performance limitations in specific workloads. LLM text generation benchmarks are weak to poor, with the small 135M model achieving 40.59 tokens/sec (bottom 10%) and the medium 7B model reaching 6.82 tokens/sec (bottom 25%). However, prompt processing speeds remain average. Given the balanced CPU-to-RAM ratio, high-capacity local SSD, and strong database operation metrics, this instance is suited for relational databases, enterprise applications, and general-purpose workloads requiring substantial local storage.
